procedure.description: pembrolizumab injection, 200 mg, first-line therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for HCPCS J9271 (pembrolizumab injection, 200 mg, first-line therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer) with date of service 2026-04-02. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish that the coverage criteria for pembrolizumab in this indication are met.

criteria.text: Histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer that is metastatic (stage IV) or recurrent and not amenable to curative treatment.
PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50 percent or greater for single-agent therapy (1 percent or greater when combined with platinum chemotherapy).
No EGFR sensitizing mutation and no ALK rearrangement, since targeted therapy is first-line for those tumors.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0 to 2.
No prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease.

chart.text: Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.6, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 50. Repeat in a year.
Blood pressure check. 132 over 85 today, 124 over 89 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Vitamin D came back 14. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. His history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Core needle biopsy, right upper lobe mass: adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative. Consistent with primary lung adenocarcinoma.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

PET/CT: 5.3 centimeter hypermetabolic right upper lobe mass, hypermetabolic right hilar and subcarinal nodes, two hypermetabolic hepatic lesions in segments 6 and 7, and a lytic hypermetabolic lesion in the left iliac wing. Stage IV disease.

PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (22C3): tumor proportion score 90 percent. Next-generation sequencing: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET exon 14, RET, and NTRK: no actionable alteration detected. Tumor mutational burden 9 per megabase.

Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

62 year old man seen in medical oncology with his son. Presented with three months of cough and 10 pounds of weight loss. Long discussion of goals: he wants treatment aimed at living longer and feeling well. Former smoker, 48 pack years, quit 5 years ago. His history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypertension on lisinopril. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works in an office. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with liver and bone metastases. Not a surgical or curative radiation candidate. ECOG 1. Still working part time, walks the dog every morning, some fatigue by evening and a cough. No prior systemic therapy. This is first-line treatment for metastatic disease.

Thoracic tumor board. Case presented. Consensus: single-agent immunotherapy first-line given the biomarker profile and performance status, palliative radiation to the iliac lesion if it becomes painful. Molecular results reviewed by the group.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Back to review the plan. Consented for pembrolizumab 200 milligrams every 3 weeks. Reviewed immune-related side effects, what to call about, and the port placement scheduled for later this week. Vitals today 117 over 72, pulse 71.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Infusion visit, cycle 1 day 1. Vitals stable, labs acceptable, pembrolizumab 200 milligrams intravenous over 30 minutes, tolerated without reaction. Return in 3 weeks.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
